label: Refund not received / defective product or service

entries.title: Who is a consumer
entries.summary: Anyone who buys goods or hires a service for a price (online or offline) for personal use is a 'consumer'. Buying for resale or commercial purpose is generally excluded.
entries.use_when: Confirming the user can use consumer law.
entries.caveat: Purchases for business/resale may not qualify.

entries.title: Deficiency in service
entries.summary: Any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality or manner of a service, including not giving a promised refund, counts as 'deficiency'. A defective product is covered as a 'defect' under Section 2(10).
entries.use_when: Refund not processed, bad service, defective product.

entries.title: Filing a complaint with the District Commission
entries.summary: A consumer can file a complaint with the District Consumer Commission, including electronically. Under the 2019 Act you can file where you live or work, not only where the seller is. Online filing is on the e-Jagriti portal (e-jagriti.gov.in), which replaced e-Daakhil from January 2025. A lawyer is not compulsory.
entries.caveat: Portal names change; tell the user to check e-jagriti.gov.in.
entries.verified_via: News reports on e-Jagriti launch Jan 2025 (checked 2026-11-08)

entries.act: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021
entries.title: Which commission (by amount paid)
entries.summary: Where the price paid is up to Rs 50 lakh, the complaint goes to the District Commission; above Rs 50 lakh up to Rs 2 crore to the State Commission; above Rs 2 crore to the National Commission.
entries.caveat: Based on value of goods/services paid, not compensation claimed.

entries.act: Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020
entries.cite: Rule 7, Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020
entries.title: Filing fee
entries.summary: No filing fee for complaints where the amount paid is up to Rs 5 lakh. Small fees apply above that (for example Rs 200 for Rs 5-10 lakh).
entries.caveat: Fee table as amended in 2022; check the portal for the current fee.
entries.verified_via: 2022 Amendment Rules fee table per secondary sources (checked 2026-11-08)

entries.title: Time limit: 2 years
entries.summary: A consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. Late complaints are accepted only if the Commission is satisfied there was sufficient cause for the delay.
entries.use_when: Always mention the deadline; flag a lawyer if near or past 2 years.

entries.title: Online platforms must answer complaints
entries.summary: Every e-commerce platform must have a grievance officer (contact shown on the website/app), who must acknowledge your complaint within 48 hours and resolve it within one month.
entries.use_when: Online purchase refund/defect: escalate to the platform's grievance officer first.

entries.title: Free pre-litigation helpline
entries.summary: The government's National Consumer Helpline (call 1915, 8am-8pm, or WhatsApp 8800001915, or consumerhelpline.gov.in) forwards your complaint to the company and often gets refunds without a case. It is a free pre-litigation step.
entries.use_when: First escalation for any consumer issue.

proof_checklist: Screenshots of the product listing and promises made
All emails, chats and complaint/ticket numbers with the seller or platform
lawyer_triggers: Close to or past the 2-year limit
Money taken through a scam/fraud (this is a cyber-crime matter: call 1930)
